questions.stem:
What does this program print?

```python
a = [4, 1, 3, 2]
a.sort()
total = 0
for x in a[:2]:
    total += x
print(total)
```
questions.explain: After sorting, a = [1, 2, 3, 4]. The slice a[:2] is [1, 2], and they add up to 3.

questions.stem: Let r(item) = v / w. The items (v, w) are P = (60, 10), Q = (100, 20) and R = (120, 30). Which item has the largest r?
questions.explain: r(P) = 6, r(Q) = 5 and r(R) = 4, so P has the largest value of r.

questions.stem: An algorithm sorts n numbers in O(n log n) time and then scans the sorted list once in O(n) time. What is the total running time?
questions.explain: The total is n log n + n, and the larger term n log n dominates, so the cost is O(n log n).
